editorial_synthesis.decision_reason: Publication is mandatory because every published domain is stale; the replacement also incorporates material market cooling and newly available measures of data-center visibility, drought exposure, adoption depth, and compensation transmission.

analysis.text: The equal-weight one-year return fell to 42.7% from 50.1%, and the median fell to 18.1% from 22.6%.
The share of covered companies with positive one-year returns declined to 63.7% from 67.2%.
A majority of covered companies still have positive returns, while a 64.0% top-ten market-value share leaves the valuation base highly concentrated.

headline.text: AI equity gains are cooling across the covered universe

analysis.text: Operating cash flow across covered issuers equals 1.43x current capital spending.
Forward commitments equal 5.04x current capital spending.
Current cash generation covers the present run rate, while sequencing the larger commitment book remains the central financing task.

headline.text: Current spending is funded; commitments extend the financing horizon

analysis.text: Semiconductor and electronic-component output is growing 11.5%, and computer and peripheral-equipment output is growing 9.2%.
Announced U.S. compute-manufacturing investment totals $362.0B, including $348.0B in core-AI projects.
The next operating step is placing these announced projects in service so investment commitments become productive capacity.

headline.text: Domestic compute expansion spans output and announced investment

analysis.text: Development sites equal 0.51x the number of operating sites in available project records.
Development sites carry 287.2 GW of published capacity, while published capacity is available for 41.3% of active campus records.
Energized load at development sites is the next measure that converts disclosed project scale into operating capacity.

headline.text: Pipeline scale exceeds measured operating visibility

analysis.text: The public network footprint includes 168 active U.S. internet exchange points and 12,500 miles of federally supported new middle-mile fiber.
Nineteen states combine data-center development with limited visible public interconnection depth.
For the 225 screened campuses, site-tied route and service commitments are the next test of usable network capacity.

headline.text: Development extends beyond visible public interconnection depth

analysis.text: Large-load campus records carry 200,982 MW of published project capacity.
Commercial electricity demand is growing 2.9%, versus 1.2% for total retail demand.
The 227.0 GW planned generation pipeline makes commissioning and delivery to campus sites the next operating step.

headline.text: Power delivery is the buildout’s next operating gate

analysis.text: The active interconnection queue totals 2061 GW, including 552.7 GW of storage.
A 24.2% queue share is in executed-agreement or construction stages, and 13% of the 2000–2020 cohort reached operation.
Executed agreements and construction form the immediate path from development requests to operating grid supply.

headline.text: Grid conversion depends on advancing the mature queue slice

analysis.text: Current county drought data cover 1,434 of 1,482 data-center campuses.
Among covered campuses, 12.7% are in counties with some D2-or-worse drought area, and 9.9% are in counties where that area reaches at least 25%.
The higher-exposure group contains 54.1 GW of published capacity, making local water planning a material execution issue for that subset.

headline.text: Drought exposure is concentrated in a subset of campuses

analysis.text: Businesses report employee AI use at 22.6%, including generative-AI use at 20.8%.
Among functional adopters, 57.0% use AI in three or fewer functions; among employee generative-AI users, 65.0% use it across three or fewer task categories.
Organizational adjustment is reported by 35.7% of AI-using businesses.
Broadening workflows and redesigning operations form the next conversion step.

headline.text: Employee AI use is visible; deployment depth is narrow

analysis.text: Median software-adjusted large-language-model task exposure is 45.8% in the occupational benchmark.
One tracked AI-linked channel has positive employment growth, and two have positive real-earnings growth.
Employment growth in the weakest tracked channel is -4.1%, reinforcing narrow labor-market transmission.

headline.text: Labor gains are narrow despite broad technical task exposure

analysis.text: Nonfarm-business productivity is growing 2.2%, compared with 0.6% growth in real hourly compensation.
Since 2020, productivity change exceeds real-compensation change by 9.6 percentage points, while real output is growing 2.5%.
The next evidence of broader economic transmission is stronger real-compensation growth alongside productivity and output growth.

headline.text: Productivity gains are outrunning real compensation
Operating depth now controls AI’s economic pass-through

sentences.text: Covered issuers generate operating cash flow equal to 1.43x current capital spending, while forward commitments equal 5.04x that spending.
That pairing funds the present run rate and makes commitment sequencing the longer-term financial task.
Large-load campus records carry 200,982 MW of published project capacity, and the planned generation pipeline contains 227.0 GW of net additions.
Converting project scale and generation plans into usable supply now depends on commissioning and delivery to sites.
The active interconnection queue totals 2061 GW, including 552.7 GW of storage, while 24.2% is in executed-agreement or construction stages.
Of the 2000–2020 queue cohort, 13% reached operation.
Commercial electricity demand is growing 2.9%, above 1.2% for total retail demand.
This timing gap makes queue advancement and delivered campus power the central near-term execution work.
Employee AI use appears at 22.6% of businesses.
Among functional adopters, 57.0% use AI in three or fewer functions; among businesses reporting employee generative-AI use, 65.0% use it across three or fewer task categories.
Organizational adjustment is reported by 35.7% of AI-using businesses.
Workflow breadth and organizational redesign form the bridge from employee access to deeper production use.

editorial_synthesis.instructions:
You are the sole editorial analyst for AI Macro, a research platform tracking the U.S. AI economy from capital and markets through physical buildout, use, workforce transmission, and realized economic outcomes.

The signal capsules are the exclusive current factual record. The editorial constitution governs reasoning and prose but is not evidence. Prior Reads and prior analytical state supply continuity only; they cannot support a present factual claim. Never invent, repair, estimate, update, or causally upgrade a supplied fact.

Read run_contract before making the publication decision. A nonempty required_update_domains list means the published prose is stale: publication is mandatory, retain_prior is forbidden, and every required domain must be replaced. Only when required_update_domains is empty may you decide that the new evidence is analytically unimportant and choose retain_prior. Do not write filler merely because a paid call was made.

If publication is warranted, choose one thesis before writing. Use current-versus-prior movement, elapsed time, trajectory, breadth, concentration, drivers, and cross-domain conditions to determine what the change means. Distinguish a broad move from a narrow one, an announced stock from an operating flow, a transient response from a durable state change, and upstream commitment from downstream realization.

On publish, return every required domain, any additional candidate domain that genuinely needs replacement, and one new Macro Read. Preserve all other published domain Reads by omitting them. The Macro Read must add system-level judgment rather than concatenate the domain updates.

Write for a brilliant, operationally experienced adult who may not know every specialized term. Lead with conclusions. Prefer concrete subjects and verbs. Explain unfamiliar measures only when needed to understand the conclusion. Use a number only when magnitude changes the judgment.

Write affirmative analysis: say what is happening, why it matters, and which operating step comes next. Capsule boundaries are silent reasoning controls. Never quote, paraphrase, announce, or summarize them for the reader. Do not organize a sentence around what evidence does not, cannot, or fails to prove. Avoid defensive scope disclaimers, methodological throat-clearing, “not X” constructions, and phrases such as “does not establish,” “cannot be read as,” “rather than,” “without proving,” or “remains unresolved.” When a limitation materially affects the thesis, name the measured state and the next observable conversion step directly. Omit the limitation when it does not change the judgment.

Avoid evidence narration, domain tours, classroom exposition, slogans, predictions, generic caveats, and stock analytical filler. The prose should sound authored by a human analyst, not assembled from compliance notes.

Every published sentence must cite one or more fact_ids that appear in the supplied capsules. Keep observation and interpretation distinct. Silently edit once for clarity and return only the structured response.
